29yn:
The Bachelor of Biomedical Science at Federation University Australia provides a comprehensive foundation in human biology and medical science, preparing students for careers in healthcare, research, and laboratory science.

Students study core areas such as anatomy, physiology, microbiology, biochemistry, pathology, and molecular biology, gaining both theoretical knowledge and practical laboratory experience. The program emphasizes scientific inquiry, critical thinking, and hands‑on skills essential for understanding human health and disease.

Graduates are prepared for roles in medical laboratories, research institutions, biotechnology companies, and healthcare sectors, or for further study in fields such as medicine, pharmacy, or allied health professions.
29t9:
The Bachelor of Business is a contemporary degree developed in collaboration with industry and designed to meet the needs of businesses now and in the future. Businesses are facing an unprecedented number of challenges and opportunities stemming from digital disruption and the rapid adoption of new technologies. There has never been a more exciting time to start a career in business, whether students are looking for a career in the corporate world or aspiring to be an entrepreneur.

With close ties to industry and a strong focus on real-world work experience, Federation Business School is renowned for producing job-ready graduates by providing students with industry placements, internships, and real-life projects during their studies. Graduates gain a solid foundation in business management, entrepreneurship, critical thinking, teamwork, leadership, creativity and innovation, and interpersonal skills. These skills are in high demand from employers and central to succeeding in the rapidly changing business world.

Federation Business School’s undergraduates complete a common first year by studying foundation business courses in:

Management

Marketing

Creativity

Innovation

Accounting and Finance

Economics

Statistics

Law.

After the first year, students will have the flexibility to switch to any undergraduate degree at Federation Business School.

From the second year, students will choose a major stream of study (specialisation) in Management, Marketing or Banking and Finance. They will also select interdisciplinary electives such as Information Technology, Psychology, Sociology, Environmental Science and/or Outdoor Studies, depending on their interests.

Students could also gain valuable experience through an overseas study tour to Nepal, Samoa or Fiji (subject to COVID travel restrictions) through the New Colombo Plan (NCP). The NCP is an initiative of the Australian Government which aims to lift knowledge of the Indo-Pacific in Australia by supporting Australian undergraduates to study in the region.

29wt: Students will learn to deliver the highest quality care that's focused on the person and use reasoning and evidence-based care to improve their patients' outcomes. Subjects include working with diverse communities, mental health, medical and surgical nursing, and palliative care. They'll also learn skills like leadership and management to give them even more confidence when they start their career. Their options will be wide when they graduate. Students may choose to work in emergency illness, mental health, long-term care, intercultural health or population health. Wherever they work, chances are your career in nursing will be challenging, stimulating and rewarding. Students may even decide to further their studies into a specialised nursing area including midwifery or paramedicine. 29yk:
Program Description

The Bachelor of Psychological Sciences is accredited with the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council (APAC) and explores a range of subjects on human thought and behaviour including developmental psychology, cognitive psychology, social psychology, abnormal psychology and personality.

Throughout their studies, students will develop a solid foundation to equip them with the communication, research, critical thinking and problem-solving skills required to meet the high demand for graduates in psychology. They will also broaden their knowledge with elective subjects throughout first, second and third year. As a graduate, students may work in community welfare and case management, business and industry, youth and family support, the criminal justice system, marketing or research.
29yp:
The Bachelor of Science provides a foundation in scientific practice and a specialisation in at least one discipline area chosen from thirteen major study areas. The program is delivered in small applied laboratory classes and workshops, allowing the development of advanced skills sought by employers. The emphasis is on acquiring skills in scientific communication, data analysis and quantitative literacy, problem solving and research skills, and a comprehensive understanding of the scientific and ethical framework of at least one major study area.

Graduates have the opportunity to undertake a research-based honours program to enhance their employment prospects and postgraduate study opportunities. Majors: Biochemistry, Biological science, Biotechnology, Behavioural Science, Chemistry, Earth materials, Ecology, Environmental geoscience, Environmental restoration, Exercise Science, Food science (minor at Gippsland, major at Ballarat), Health and nutrition, Mathematics (major at Ballarat, minor at Gippsland), Microbiology, Mineral processing.
6iu2:
The Bachelor of Science (Environmental Science) is an undergraduate program that explores the scientific principles underlying environmental systems and sustainability. It prepares students to understand, assess, and address environmental challenges such as climate change, pollution, biodiversity loss, and resource management.

Students study core areas including ecology, environmental chemistry, geology, hydrology, climate science, and environmental policy, gaining both theoretical knowledge and practical skills. The curriculum emphasizes fieldwork, laboratory analysis, data interpretation, and environmental monitoring, enabling students to evaluate environmental impacts and develop sustainable solutions.

The program integrates interdisciplinary approaches, combining natural sciences with policy and management perspectives to address complex environmental issues at local, national, and global levels.

Graduates are prepared for careers in environmental consulting, conservation, government agencies, sustainability management, and resource planning, or for further study in environmental science, engineering, or policy.
94xe:
The Bachelor of Science (Veterinary Bioscience) is an undergraduate program that provides a strong foundation in animal biology, health, and disease, preparing students for careers in veterinary science, animal health, and related biomedical fields. The program integrates scientific theory with practical applications to develop an understanding of the biological systems that underpin animal health and welfare.

Students study key areas such as animal anatomy and physiology, microbiology, genetics, biochemistry, immunology, and pathology, along with principles of animal nutrition, disease prevention, and veterinary practices. The curriculum emphasizes laboratory work, scientific research, and critical analysis, enabling students to apply knowledge in real‑world contexts.

The program is ideal for students aiming to pursue veterinary medicine, animal care professions, or research roles in animal and biomedical sciences. It also provides a pathway to further postgraduate study in veterinary science or related disciplines.

Graduates are prepared for careers in animal health industries, veterinary support services, research laboratories, pharmaceutical companies, and agricultural sectors, or for progression to professional veterinary programs (subject to further requirements).

Program Description

This program provides an opportunity for students to develop an advanced understanding of data science by interpreting and synthesising complex information, concepts and theories to relevant disciplines, using data science tools and methods to manage, process, and analyse data.

Throughout the program, students will utilise their skills to handle large volumes of data, working with real-time data, cloud computing, unstructured data and statistical models. As a graduate, students may work in data science related areas such as the health care, finance, government administration and IT industries.
8dqn: The Master of Data Science will equip students with a comprehensive suite of skills needed to manage, manipulate, analyze, and visualize data across a wide range of sectors, including science, business, IT, healthcare, and government. Their studies will include a deep dive into areas such as artificial intelligence and machine learning, data analytics for cyber threat intelligence, experiment design and visualization, programming, and more.
7rko: In this Master of Digital Business Transformation degree students learn how university's digital-focused world impacts the success of business and business practices. They will develop specialized learning in digital transformation through a variety of cross-disciplinary units, including IT project management, business economics, professional research communication, service design, international marketing, and more.
29u4:
Civil engineers are responsible for the design and construction of all types of structures including single to multi-storied buildings, roads, dams, bridges, pipelines, towers, harbours, airports and railways. Civil engineers also plan, design and test the infrastructure associated with transport, gas supply, water supply and sewerage systems.

As a graduate, students' advanced skills together with the knowledge and appreciation of the environment, sustainable development, as well as social and political aspects, will impact their work as a civil engineer.

Graduates of this program may be employed in managerial roles with private consultants, contracting companies, or federal, state and local government organisations.

There are significant opportunities for employment in Australia, as well as in South-East Asia and throughout the rest of the world.
29u5:
Mechanical engineering focuses on applying the principles of physics and mechanical science to the design, development, and operation of mechanical systems. The program provides comprehensive coverage of areas such as design, research, evaluation, manufacture, installation, testing, operation, maintenance, and management of machines and systems.

Areas of study and application include, but are not limited to, mechanical and mechatronic systems, automated and robotic devices, heat transfer processes, thermodynamic and combustion systems, and fluid and thermal energy systems.

Graduates of this program are eligible for membership with Engineers Australia and are well prepared for managerial and professional roles in private consultancy firms, contracting companies, or government organisations at the federal, state, and local levels. Employment opportunities for mechanical engineers are strong both within Australia and internationally, particularly across South-East Asia and other global regions.
29yz:
The Master of Philosophy (MPhil) is a higher degree by research that is completed entirely through independent inquiry. Graduates of the program demonstrate an advanced and integrated understanding of a complex and specialised body of knowledge.

Typically completed over two years of full-time study, the MPhil requires candidates to show their capacity for independent research through the submission of a substantial thesis or, where applicable, a portfolio of creative works accompanied by an exegesis. Throughout the research process, candidates are guided and supported by an academic supervisory team.

Within this program, candidates undertake a research project within the broad fields of business, management, and commerce.

29ug:
Program Description

Be an advocate for social justice and human rights. Make a real difference to the lives of people in need. Excel in their career in one of the fastest growing professions. Students might be a new graduate looking for a clear career path or an experienced social worker wanting to take the next step in their professional life. Or perhaps students are ready for a career change and want to step into social work.

Whatever their background, faculty will prepare students to work across human and community services in government bodies, non-government organisations, community and health services and more. They'll become confident working with migrants, people with alcohol, drug and mental health problems and in palliative care, child protection, youth services and much more.

They'll be exposed to challenging real life situations through 140 days during your studies in social work settings, being mentored by experienced professionals in the field. Then, once they graduate, they can go on to be a qualified social worker, take up management positions or work in national or international policy development. This is an Australian Association of Social Workers (AASW) accredited qualification, and is an entry qualification into the social work profession. It has been deemed to meet the Australian Social Work Education and Accreditation Standards.
